status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The operator suspended local service after the collision. This demonstrates a concrete restriction on operation in response to a safety concern. It does not establish fault or a complete recovery criterion.

review.requirement_proposition: AI systems should remain robust, secure and safe throughout their entire lifecycle, functioning appropriately without unreasonable safety or security risks under normal use, foreseeable use or misuse and other adverse conditions.
review.reason_for_change: The reported robotaxi collision injured two pedestrians. The driving mode, active automation stack and control telemetry are not available, so the evidence does not resolve the AI system’s role in the collision or its safety-control outcome.

conclusion_change.previous: The collision produced material physical harm, but the evidence does not establish the perception, planning, control or human-supervision mechanism needed for a Failure Class mapping. Material collision harm remains separate from unresolved nonactivation/effectiveness. Driving mode, active stack and safety-control telemetry are unavailable; local suspension does not establish fault or a complete recovery criterion.
conclusion_change.new: The collision and hospital treatment are reported, and local service was suspended. The operational restriction is supported. The AI safety outcome remains unresolved because driving mode and control telemetry are unavailable; suspension does not establish fault.
